title: stream-shelve-resume-lease-renegotiation-openai-adapter
author: Maya Khatri
release_notes: Introduces a server-side "shelve" lifecycle for streaming sessions to enable short-term disconnect/resume semantics, lease renegotiation, and idempotent tool-call guarantees via idempotency tokens. Backwards compatible with existing OpenAI-compat streaming clients; opt-in via header or adapter flag.
description: Motivation: We frequently see production customers hit transient network glitches and orchestrator preemption that cause client disconnects during long-running streaming sessions. Immediate abort semantics cause tool-call duplication risk or poor UX when clients reconnect. This change introduces a short-lived "shelve" state for streams: the server holds minimal session state and a lease token, allowing clients to reconnect and resume within a renegotiated lease window. The approach reduces duplicated tool/function calls, improves perceived stability, and keeps the OpenAI-compat interface stable.

d6a9ff2 SDK-TS: expose resume token and reconnect helper for streams

review_comments: Diego Ramos: This looks good overall. Please clarify eviction TTL semantics and add a metric for shelved_session_count.
Maya Khatri: Added metric 'stream.shelved.count' and documented TTL behavior in docs/streaming-lifecycle.md. Reply: TTL is 30s by default with a config knob per deployment tier.
Evan Liu: We need to ensure function/tool calls are idempotent across resume. Can you add idempotency keys at the adapter boundary and instrument the DB checks?
Maya Khatri: Implemented idempotency keys generated from (session_id, tool_call_id, attempt) and persisted a lightweight tombstone record; added tests for duplicate replay prevention.
Priya Natarajan: What about blowups where the shelved payload is large? Consider trimming cached KV/attachments on shelve to keep memory under control.

Maya Khatri: Shelved state is intentionally minimal: only in-flight tool-call metadata, last ack offset, and a compact resume token. Large attachments continue to be stored externally and are referenced by pointer. Documented in the design section.
design_summary: Introduce a three-state stream lifecycle: active -> shelved -> tombstoned. On client cancel or unexpected disconnect, the server optionally transitions the session to shelved instead of immediately aborting. Shelved sessions carry a lease token and minimal replay metadata. Clients that reconnect present the lease token in a resume handshake; the server renegotiates a new, shorter lease if capacity permits and reattaches the in-memory KV cache or replays from persisted checkpoints. If the lease expires or the session is explicitly abandoned, the tombstone path cleans up any transient markers and finalizes tool-call outcomes.
backwards_compatibility: Behavior is opt-in at the adapter level. Existing clients continue to receive immediate abort semantics unless they opt in via the X-Redwood-Shelve: true header or by enabling the shelve flag in the OpenAI-compat adapter. No breaking changes to the streaming message envelope or existing function-call fields. SDK helpers add convenience methods but are not required.
testing_and_qa: Added comprehensive unit tests for shelve state transitions, idempotent tool-call handling, and lease expiry. Integration tests simulate intermittent network loss and verify no duplicate external tool executions. E2E tests run against a staging cluster with the shelve flag toggled on and off. Load tests show <5% p99 latency regression under typical traffic; per-token cost unchanged. Observability: new metrics stream.shelved.count, stream.shelve_lease_renegotiation.rate, and trace spans for resume handshake.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag 'enable_stream_shelve' and OpenAI-compat adapter opt-in. Rollout: 1) Merge behind flag, 2) enable for internal canary traffic (10% of requests) and monitor metrics/alerts for failed resumes and duplicated tool calls, 3) increase to 50% then full. Alerting: >0.1% duplicate-tool-call rate or shelved_session_count growth > 3x baseline triggers rollback.
compat_adapter_changes: OpenAI-compat adapter now accepts X-Redwood-Shelve and translates to internal shelve negotiation. Added header negotiation for resume_token in initial handshake and semantics for 'resume_candidate' vs 'fresh' stream. Documented adapter behavior in docs and updated openapi examples to show resume flow.
observability: New metrics: stream.shelved.count (gauge), stream.shelve.lease_renegotiation.success (counter), stream.shelve.resume_latency_ms (histogram). Added traces: shelve.create, shelve.resume.handshake, shelve.expire. Dashboard saved as 'Streaming > Shelve Lifecycle'.
manual_steps: Operators: to adjust default TTL set STREAM_SHELVE_TTL in config. To inspect shelved sessions: redis-cli HGETALL shelved:<session_id>. To force-abandon a shelved session use POST /internal/streams/<id>/abandon.
